declaration.preface: At POLYVENTIVE LLC (GROUP), we are committed to ensuring fair and equitable wages for all employees across our operations. We recognize that every individual deserves compensation that meets basic needs and supports a dignified standard of living. This Living Wage Policy reflects our dedication to employee well-being, responsible business practices, and alignment with international labor and human rights standards. By upholding these values, Polyventive strengthens its workforce and contributes to sustainable growth in the communities where we operate.
declaration.declaration:
Polyventive LLC is dedicated to ensuring that all employees and contract workers are compensated with a living wage, defined as the minimum income necessary for workers to meet their basic needs—such as food, housing, healthcare, and education while maintaining a dignified quality of life.

Polyventive is committed to paying wages that exceed the legal minimum wage in the regions where we operate. We ensure that wages are sufficient to cover essential living expenses, promoting financial independence, stability, and overall well-being.

A living wage at Polyventive ensures that employees and contract workers can meet their fundamental needs, including food, housing, transportation, education, healthcare, and the ability to save.

Polyventive is committed to maintaining pay equity across the organization, ensuring that no employee faces wage discrimination based on gender, race, age, or any other personal characteristic.

Polyventive regularly reviews and updates its wage structures to account for changes in the cost of living, inflation, and market conditions.
declaration.scope: This policy applies to all POLYVENTIVE LLC (GROUP) employees, workers, contractors, sub-contractors, suppliers, partners, and stakeholders across all operational locations. It covers our manufacturing sites, offices, and all associated business operations, and extends to interactions with clients, vendors, regulators, and the wider community.

definitions.title: Living Wage Definition & Methodology
definitions.content:
Polyventive LLC is dedicated to ensuring that all employees and contract workers are compensated with a living wage, defined as the minimum income necessary for workers to meet their basic needs—such as food, housing, healthcare, and education while maintaining a dignified quality of life.

A living wage at Polyventive ensures that employees and contract workers can meet their fundamental needs, including food, housing, transportation, education, healthcare, and the ability to save.

We assess local living conditions and set wages that accurately reflect the true cost of living in each region.

Polyventive regularly reviews and updates its wage structures to account for changes in the cost of living, inflation, and market conditions. In specific business units, targeted wage assessments may focus on selected employee groups, but the full living wage policy applies globally to all internal employees and contract workers.

Establish Year 2022 as the baseline year for tracking Polyventive’s living wage compliance and overall employee compensation performance.

The Living Wage Policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources Department in collaboration with the Compliance Team. This review will assess progress towards achieving the defined targets, evaluate the policy's effectiveness, and ensure alignment with evolving legal requirements and industry best practices in labour rights.

focusAreas: Wage Equity and Gender Pay Parity

Living Wage Implementation: We conduct annual wage reviews to ensure that both our internal employees and contract workers in selected business units are earning a living wage. These reviews take into account local living costs, inflation rates, and prevailing economic conditions, allowing us to align compensation fairly with the realities of our workforce.
Wage Equity and Gender Pay Parity: Polyventive is committed to maintaining pay equity across the organization, ensuring that no employee faces wage discrimination based on gender, race, age, or any other personal characteristic. We uphold the principle of fair and equal pay for all employees and contract workers performing similar roles with comparable qualifications and experience.

We regularly carry out pay equity audits to confirm that no wage disparities exist on the basis of gender, race, or other discriminatory factors among our employees and contract workers. Whenever gaps are identified, we take prompt corrective action and share findings with management to drive continuous improvement.
Employee Awareness and Engagement: We maintain a transparent and accessible communication channel where employees and contract workers can raise wage-related concerns, such as inequity or unfair compensation. This platform enables proactive resolution and reinforces our commitment to fair and equitable pay practices across all levels of the organization.

Our Living Wage Policy is publicly available on our website and shared internally through employee handbooks, newsletters, and training sessions. This ensures that all employees and contract workers are informed and aware of our commitment.
Governance and Monitoring: We actively engage with suppliers and contractors to make sure they fully understand living wage expectations. We provide training and guidance on wage equity, ethical wage practices, and human rights standards, enabling them to meet our requirements effectively.
Annual Wage Reviews: Polyventive regularly reviews and updates its wage structures to account for changes in the cost of living, inflation, and market conditions.
